To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed FPGA-based system for SVM training achieves a 10x speedup over the best GPU-based implementation, and a 30x speedup over state-of-the-art CPUs.

the proposed FPGA-based system achieves more than 10× higher throughput compared to the fastest GPU-based implementation, and more than an order-of-magnitude higher compared to the fastest CPU-based implementation.

we propose and implement a FPGA-based SVM training framework for nonlinear SVMs that is able to train on large datasets, is scalable and is able to achieve more than an order magnitude better performance compared to state-of the art CPU and GPU based implementations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new paradigm for SVM training that is scalable to very large problems.
the development of an FPGA-based system for training nonlinear SVM classifiers, which can be used in a variety of applications such as image classification, object detection, or bioinformatics.
the design and evaluation of a complete FPGA-based nonlinear SVM training system using ensemble learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the FPGA implementation of the nonlinear SVM training using an ensemble approach has shown to be a viable alternative to the state-of-the-art implementations in terms of both performance and scalability.
this paper presents the first FPGA-based implementation of nonlinear SVM training using the ensemble learning approach.
the proposed FPGA implementation achieves the best performance in terms of throughput, energy and power consumption, while the CPU and GPU implementations are better in terms of cost and latency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed system can be applied to large datasets and can achieve a speedup of up to 3 orders of magnitude compared to the best GPU implementation.
we have designed a complete system for training SVM classifiers using ensemble learning and FPGA.
we have presented a complete FPGA-based framework for nonlinear SVM training.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed system can be used to solve large-scale nonlinear SVM problems in a fraction of time required by current state-of-the-art solutions.
the proposed FPGA-based system is able to train large-scale nonlinear SVMs in real-time and with high accuracy.
FPGA can be an excellent choice for SVM training, especially for large-scale problems, and can provide significant speedups compared to state-of the art GPU and CPU-based implementations.
